name: Mentimeter
tagline: Presentation tool where the audience votes, answers quizzes and fills word clouds live from their phones.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core mechanic is not hard: a room code, a phone-friendly voting page, a websocket pushing counts to a projected bar chart or word cloud. An agent can get multiple-choice, scales, word clouds and open-text working in one session, and for a classroom or a team offsite that is genuinely enough. What breaks is everything around it: you need a public URL and TLS so phones can actually reach it, you need the join flow to be idiot-proof in front of 80 people, and you need the result chart to not look like a hackathon demo when it is on a 4 metre screen. Mentimeter's real product is twenty question types, template libraries, PowerPoint and Slides embedding, and the confidence that it will not fall over mid-keynote. Build it for your own talks, do not build it for the company all-hands.
coreLoopDIY: Runs a self-hosted presenter deck with a room code, where audience phones submit votes over websockets and slides render live results as bars, scales or word clouds.
requirements: a small VPS or tunnel with a public HTTPS URL, phones will not join localhost
a short memorable domain, people type the join link by hand
a projector test run before you rely on it
whatYouLose: Twenty-plus question types: ranking, 2x2 grids, pin on image, Q and A moderation, quiz leaderboards with timing
PowerPoint and Google Slides integration, so your polls live inside the deck you already made
Template galleries and design presets that make the output look deliberate
Reliability and capacity at hundreds of concurrent voters, plus someone to blame when it breaks
Export, reporting and comparing results across sessions over time
moatNotes: Not a network moat: the audience never signs up, they just type a code. The moat is that it works flawlessly in a high-stakes room, which is boring and expensive.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the moment of truth is live and public. A broken poll in front of a room of paying conference attendees costs more than a decade of subscription, so presenters buy insurance, not features. Mentimeter also wins on breadth: by the time you have hand-built ranking, quiz scoring, Q and A moderation and a slide embed for PowerPoint, you have spent a month on something that was never your job. The personal build makes sense for recurring low-stakes rooms you control, a class, a workshop, a weekly team session.
notes: Fine for a classroom, risky for a keynote. The gap is not code, it is the nerve to run it live.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted live audience polling tool, like a minimal Mentimeter, in an empty folder.

Stack, no substitutions: Node 20 with Express, the ws package for websockets, SQLite via better-sqlite3, server-rendered HTML with plain CSS and vanilla JS. No React, no build step, no bundler, no external CDN.

Data model: a session has an id, a 5-digit numeric join code, a title and an ordered list of slides. A slide has a type (one of: multiple_choice, scale_1_5, word_cloud, open_text), a question, and options for multiple_choice. Votes store session id, slide id, a voter token from a cookie, and a value.

Routes:
- GET / : list sessions, form to create one.
- GET /s/:id/edit : add, reorder and delete slides. Plain forms, full page reloads are fine.
- GET /s/:id/present : presenter view. Huge type, dark background, shows the current slide, the join URL and the join code, a live result chart, a live voter count, and next/prev controls. Presenter sends slide changes over the websocket.
- GET /join : code entry form. GET /j/:code : audience voting view, mobile first, large tap targets, follows whatever slide the presenter is on, confirms the vote and locks that slide for that voter token.
- Results render in the page with CSS only: horizontal bars for choices and scales, scaled inline text for word clouds, a scrolling list for open text.

Websockets: one channel per session. Audience sends votes, server writes to SQLite then broadcasts aggregated counts to presenter and audience. Never broadcast raw voter tokens. Rejoin must resync state after a refresh or a dropped connection.

Also include: a reset-votes button per slide, CSV export of raw results, and a /seed script that creates a demo session with one slide of each type.

Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, email, payments, quiz scoring and leaderboards, PowerPoint or Google Slides integration, image upload, telemetry, analytics.

Config in .env: PORT, PUBLIC_BASE_URL, ADMIN_PASSWORD. Protect / and all edit and present routes with HTTP basic auth using ADMIN_PASSWORD; audience routes stay public. Commit a .env.example, never a .env.

Write a README that states plainly: this needs a public HTTPS URL for phones to join, test the projector and the join flow before a real session, and it is sized for roughly 100 concurrent voters on one process.

Finish with a load check script that simulates 100 voters hitting one slide, and report the result in the README.
